A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HypDAE and contain readable main texts and complete appendices. Their shared framework, benchmarks, equations, and retained figures support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation results, four-dataset FID/LPIPS comparisons, ablations, and a 30-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation and user-study results and adds Euclidean, pseudo-label, CLIP-similarity, and loss-weight experiments.

M1.justification: v2 removes Stage III's Hyperbolic Delta Mapper and text-guided inference, replacing the three-stage framework with two stages and adding CLIP/DeepFace pseudo-label training. It also describes the Stage-I adapter as a five-layer MLP rather than v1's Transformer, although one older Transformer statement remains.

E1.justification: The text-instructed editing task evaluated in v1 Section 4.4 and Figure 12 disappears from v2, substantially narrowing task coverage. Animal Faces, Flowers, VGGFaces, NABirds, FFHQ, and the appendix's DomainNet style scenarios remain; pseudo-label experiments use retained datasets.

E2.justification: v2 adds HypDAE (Euc) to Table 1's quantitative comparison; v1 already illustrated Euclidean interpolation qualitatively. The eight external Table 1 baselines, DiffAE interpolation comparison, and user-study comparator membership are unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Euclidean and pseudo-label retraining controls, CLIP-S/CLIP-P metrics, radii 4.0 and 3.0 in the Animal Faces sweep, and a loss-weight sweep. Existing dataset splits, shot settings, image resolution, and user-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially strengthens component analysis with quantitative Euclidean-versus-hyperbolic and pseudo-versus-real-label experiments, expanded radius tests measuring identity drift, and the loss-weight ablation in appendix Figure 15. Existing stochastic-encoding, guidance, interpolation, and domain-shift analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original HypDAE scores survive unchanged as HypDAE (Real), alongside new variant results: Animal Faces FID is 20.72 for Euc and 13.14 for Pseudo, versus the retained Real value of 14.31. These are different-variant comparisons. v2 also adds pseudo-label accuracies, CLIP scores, extended radius and loss-weight results, while removing v1's text-editing examples; user-study scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit DDPM forward/reverse-process definitions and the noise-schedule formulation in appendix Section 7, and revises the stochastic-encoding expression in Equation 4. The existing hyperbolic metric, Möbius operations, exponential/logarithmic maps, and geodesic formulas are retained; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes joint text-image hierarchies and text-guided generation. v2 removes those central contributions and adds the claim that competitive few-shot generation does not require human-annotated class labels. The core claim of combining hyperbolic representations with diffusion remains.

C2.justification: v2 newly suggests that noise in human annotations explains pseudo-label benefits and interprets loss weighting as controlling semantic consistency versus diversity. Earlier interpretations of hierarchical radii, interpolation, and the limitations on clipart generation are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-access information and specifies pseudo-label construction using CLIP ViT-B/32 or DeepFace/VGG-Face with one reference image per class. Stage III implementation details are removed. Existing hardware, batch sizes, optimizers, training budgets, and hyperbolic encoder/decoder depths were already documented in v1's appendix.

R1.justification: v2 removes DeltaEdit and modality-gap connections, adds hyperbolic contrastive learning and manifold references, and explicitly distinguishes its category-level task from subject-driven diffusion customization. The principal positioning relative to HAE and DiffAE remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method exposition are extensively rewritten around the revised scope. v2 introduces separate pseudo-labeling and latent-editing subsections, promotes ablations to a standalone subsection, and adds diffusion background to the appendix. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the pipeline, adds a geometric schematic and Euclidean/loss-weight visualizations, removes the text-editing panel, and expands the result tables with a new CLIP table. The overall two-column design and most image galleries remain unchanged; late appendix galleries differ only in figure numbering.

improvement.justification: The quantitative Euclidean control addresses v1's reliance on qualitative evidence for the benefit of hyperbolic geometry, while pseudo-label and parameter studies improve validation. The narrower task presentation and added implementation information also help. These gains are limited by overbroad label-free claims—VGGFaces pseudo-labeling still uses known-class references—and inconsistent MLP/Transformer wording. Overall, v2 provides stronger support for its retained core contribution, with unresolved documentation and interpretation issues.
